brief: Northern Trust lays out the FOMC hold-vs-raise debate ahead of next week's meeting under new Chairman Kevin Warsh. Growth: aggregate demand is strong and recession risk is low, but a K-shaped split leaves rate-sensitive sectors cautious while AI-linked firms invest aggressively; Q2 GDP slowed only because of temporary drags (inventories, net exports, government spending), not weak underlying demand. Inflation: PCE is 3.7% versus a 2% target, unmet for 65 months; oil and tariff shocks look to be fading but risks stay skewed higher, and AI-buildout cost pressure could prove more persistent. Employment: 4.1% unemployment is consistent with full employment and hiring is positive, but falling participation suggests some slack. Long-term Treasury yields have risen sharply despite Treasury intervention, and a hold could accelerate that selloff. Northern Trust's own call: expects a 25 basis point hike this month to protect Fed credibility early in Warsh's tenure, then will watch whether yields stabilize to judge if one hike is enough. Five Warsh-commissioned policy task forces report around year-end.
